question.problem:
The velocity of a motorcycle, measured in meters per second, is given by the function $v(t)$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. The values of $v(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| $t$ | $0$ | $3$ | $6$ | $9$ | $12$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)$ | $0$ | $3$ | $10$ | $43$ | $70$ |

Approximate the acceleration ${v}^{′}(t)$ when $t=9$ using a backward difference approximation.
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{v}^{′}(t)≈\frac{v(t)-v(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the time $t=9.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=3.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{′}(9) & ≈\frac{v(9)-v(9-3)}{3} \\  & =\frac{v(9)-v(6)}{3} \\  & =\frac{43-10}{3} \\  & =\frac{33}{3} \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is $11\,\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2}.$
